entry.name: Data migration planner
entry.description: Plans a controlled data migration through mappings, validation, cutover, rollback, and accountable reconciliation without moving production data.
entry.audience: Engineering, data, and operations teams preparing a bounded system or schema migration.
principles: Make source-to-target semantics and ownership explicit
Prove reconciliation and rollback before cutover
Treat destructive cleanup as a separate post-verification decision
boundaries: Do not read unauthorized production data, execute migration jobs, change schemas, cut over traffic, delete sources, or bypass retention and legal holds
Do not copy credentials, personal data, or production samples into package fixtures or broad review outputs
Do not claim readiness when volume, performance, reconciliation, rollback, or owner evidence is missing
intake: Source and target systems, scope, owners, data classes, schema versions, volume, and migration objective
Field mappings, transforms, defaults, identifiers, retention, holds, quality rules, and reconciliation thresholds
Dry-run environment, cutover window, rollback trigger, approvers, downstream consumers, and evidence destination
workflow: Inventory authorized source and target contracts, owners, data classes, dependencies, and success thresholds
Define mappings, transformations, exception handling, reconciliation, performance, cutover, and rollback evidence
Populate the packaged mapping schema, cutover-readiness visual, and complete migration plan
Expose blockers and owner decisions without executing production reads, writes, schema changes, cutover, or cleanup

example.request: Prepare the migration plan for these synthetic CRM account records and supplied source/target schemas; do not access or change production.
example.outcome: A field mapping, transformation and exception contract, reconciliation thresholds, cutover-readiness visual, rollback plan, and owner handoff using synthetic evidence only.

doneWhen: Every field and record class has a source, target, transformation, default, quality rule, and accountable owner
Reconciliation, performance, rollback, holds, downstream dependencies, and destructive cleanup are explicit
The visual and Markdown plan agree on ready, blocked, untested, and owner-decision states
No production access, migration, schema mutation, cutover, deletion, or cleanup occurred
capabilityGuidance: The profile grants workspace-limited planning and inline visualization only; databases, migration runners, production schemas, traffic controls, and deletion tools remain unavailable.
Use only approved synthetic or minimized fixtures and retain the complete Markdown migration plan as fallback.

contribution.problem: Migration/cutover-adjacent entries in this catalog either model a single scoped ledger with no cross-batch snapshot binding (so a rehearsal or count could silently reference a different source/target snapshot than the one actually approved) or leave cutover readiness as a status toggle with no reconciliation math, exception disposition, or rollback-verification gate, so a cutover could be recommended without proof every rejected record was actually dispositioned and every batch actually reconciled.
contribution.repeatableJob: Given a source/target system snapshot identity, field mappings, rehearsal/production batches with row counts and checksums, controlled per-batch evidence, and dispositioned exceptions, reconcile every batch (source = migrated + rejected + held, within tolerance), require every required field to have a mapping, require every exception to be explicitly resolved with verified evidence, require a verified rollback plan, and gate cutover readiness on an independent, non-self, authority-bound approval dated after every grounding batch so the record can only report cutover-ready when every quantity, mapping, exception, and rollback claim is actually proven.
contribution.proofPlan: The packaged schema keeps the exact legacy sourceVersion/targetVersion/mappings/reconciliation object valid under anyOf (the enriched branch reuses those same field names/types at the top level so a complete enriched record also satisfies the legacy branch), while the enriched branch additionally requires systems, requiredFields, principals, evidence, exceptions, dataQualityFindings, a rollback record, a cutoverApproval, and a handoff; a total semantic validator registered in scripts/artifact-semantics.mjs enforces count/checksum reconciliation via numbersEqual, cross-batch/snapshot evidence grounding, required-field mapping coverage, unresolved-reject detection, rollback verification, and self/arbitrary-approval rejection, and a realistic synthetic CRM-migration fixture backs a focused adversarial test suite covering cross-batch/snapshot evidence, count mismatches, missing mappings, unresolved rejects, checksum mismatches, and CLI/legacy compatibility.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both are engineering-category readiness gates that turn execution evidence (rehearsal batches versus test runs) into a single accountable go/no-go recommendation before an irreversible or release-facing downstream action, and both reject self-verification.
existingAlternatives.difference: Quality assurance lead maps requirements to test-case coverage and defect verification for a repeatable release cycle, while data migration planner reconciles source-to-target record counts, checksums, and rejects for a one-time cutover; the underlying evidence shapes and reconciliation math are not interchangeable.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both bind a large batch of transformed records (translated strings versus migrated rows) to source-of-truth counts and a completeness gate before an accountable release/cutover decision.
existingAlternatives.difference: Localization program manager reconciles translation coverage and linguistic QA findings per locale, while data migration planner reconciles row/checksum control totals and rehearsal evidence per batch against a source/target snapshot identity; the domain quantities and dispositioning rules differ entirely.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both prepare a bounded, irreversible-adjacent handoff (cutover versus deployment) that treats accountable approval and evidence as the basis for a go decision without performing the action themselves.
existingAlternatives.difference: Release coordinator grounds readiness in GitHub checks, artifacts, and communication approval, not in row-count/checksum reconciliation or an explicit rollback-verification gate, which is the actual contract data migration planner models.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both produce a structured finding/exception ledger (accessibility findings versus migration exceptions) gated by an accountable reviewer distinct from the record owner before a release-facing recommendation is marked ready, and both explicitly reject a waived/unresolved item counting as clearance.
existingAlternatives.difference: Accessibility review coordinator scopes findings to WCAG success criteria and remediation verification, while data migration planner scopes findings to reject dispositioning and batch reconciliation against a source/target snapshot identity, a materially different evidence and reconciliation model.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both model a source-to-target field mapping/transform contract that must be complete and verified before an integration or migration can be considered ready.
existingAlternatives.difference: API integration engineer verifies request/response contract mappings against a live integration test suite, while data migration planner verifies row-level field mappings against reconciled batch counts and checksums for a one-time bulk migration; the two do not share an evidence or verification model.
